A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCAM research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite extensive reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting experiments on eleven real-world datasets, component ablations, and synthetic and real-series analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds measured training-resource comparisons in Appendix G.4.

M1.justification: The convolution/FFN reconstruction network, adaptive masks, joint training, and selective spectral normalization are retained. The final objective in v1 Eq. 6 matches v3 Eq. 5; removing the preliminary squared-error derivation does not establish a training-procedure change.

E1.justification: Both use four ETT datasets, Electricity, Traffic, Weather, four PeMS subsets, and the same noisy-sinusoid case study. The new efficiency evaluation reuses Electricity without introducing another task or domain.

E2.justification: MLP, CycleNet, PatchTST, and iTransformer remain the evaluated comparators, with unchanged component-ablation configurations. Newly cited architectures in the limitations section are not added to the reported experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: v3 adds resource profiling on Electricity with batch size 32, measuring parameter counts, peak allocated memory, and training time per iteration. Existing forecasting splits, horizons, metrics, optimizer settings, and early stopping remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix G.4 adds a controlled analysis of training overhead with and without SCAM across four backbones. Existing ablations, reconstruction analyses, and mask case studies are retained; the detailed SNR study moves from Section 4.2.2 to Appendix E.3.

E5.justification: Both retain the same SNR boxplot and statement about multiple random seeds, without specifying a run count. The new checklist acknowledges missing main-result error bars but adds no uncertainty estimates or significance tests.

E6.justification: All corresponding forecasting and ablation table values are unchanged. v3 Table 6 adds resource results, including training times of 6.126 ms/iteration for MLP and 30.451 ms/iteration for MLP with SCAM under the stated Electricity profiling setting.

T1.justification: v3 removes the squared-error auxiliary-loss decomposition in v1 Eq. 4 and expands the fully connected Lipschitz argument using a Taylor expansion and derivative bound in Appendix C, Eq. 10. The candidate-dataset statement is also relabeled from Proposition 1 to Hypothesis 1.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about reconstruction-based pseudo labels, adaptive masking, spectral normalization, and improved forecasting generalization. No new central contribution or demonstrated application is claimed.

C2.justification: New Appendix A explicitly discusses excluded architectures and untested LLM-scale models. Appendix G.4 interprets the measured training overhead as constant and scalable. The checklist additionally asserts that improvements exceed statistical error without quantifying that error.

D1.justification: v3 adds concrete memory, parameter-count, and training-time disclosures, together with the profiling batch size. The advertised code location changes from an anonymous link to a named GitHub repository; existing architecture hyperparameters, hardware, and training instructions are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds foundational MIL references and references supporting discussion of untested architectures and large forecasting models. It removes the AutoForecast/HIVE-COTE model-based meta-learning discussion and Senane et al. citation. The broader meta-learning and self-supervised-learning positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The introduction receives localized explanatory rewrites, related work is condensed, and the detailed SNR subsection moves to the appendix. Author information, acknowledgments, limitations, and a conference checklist are added or updated, while the main scientific section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with widespread resizing and repositioning of figures and tables. v3 introduces a new SCAM overview diagram, relocates the geometric overview and SNR figures, expands several captions, and adds the efficiency table.

improvement.justification: Measured training costs in Table 6 and explicit architecture limitations in Appendix A modestly improve practical transparency. Forecasting validation remains unchanged, some displays become more compressed, and the checklist's new assertion that gains exceed statistical error lacks supporting uncertainty estimates. These limits keep the overall improvement modest.
